title: Companies that don't do reinforcement learning may not make it through the next wave
dek: After language pretraining hit a bottleneck, the few hundred most core researchers in Silicon Valley have bet their resources on self-play RL, which trades inference compute for training compute and lets models explore logical reasoning on their own.
why: A complete breakdown of the AGI paradigm shift by a frontline Silicon Valley researcher, packed with consensus that hasn't fully spread, concrete numbers and route judgments — high information density.
who: Founders, investors and engineers watching the evolution of AGI technical routes, especially those trying to judge where the next wave of opportunity lies after pretraining.
skip: After 1:05:54, the part about basic research culture and Silicon Valley player commentary can be fast-forwarded.

points.h: The pretraining path may have already hit a bottleneck
points.body: Guangmi's judgment: there is a 50% chance that the traditional Scaling Law has already failed, and the other 50% is that continuing down the old path and throwing a hundred thousand cards at it can still lead to AGI. The two probabilities are ‘Harvard Harvard’. The evidence he sees is that all three elements — parameters, data and compute — are stuck. The best model is a 6700B-total-parameter MOE, because that is the limit of what H100s on a single server can hold; no model has been seen pushing up three to five times to two or three trillion parameters. On data, many companies have scraped 15 to 20T of high-quality text, but it is hard to increase that to 50 to 100T. On compute, the largest single H100 cluster is 32,000 cards, and there won't be a multiple-fold improvement until the B series comes out.

points.h: Multimodality and hundred-thousand-card clusters are not paradigm-level changes
points.body: Guangmi groups the alternative routes into three. The first is multimodality, especially vision: high certainty, but today there is no evidence that intelligence or logical ability emerges from training on the visual modality — Tesla FSD doesn't work when moved to another new device, there's no generalization. The second is hundred-thousand-card clusters, betting that compute decides life or death, but a 30,000-card cluster basically Bricks once every two hours, and a 100,000-card cluster Bricks once every twenty or thirty minutes; the interconnection difficulty may be more complex than SpaceX launching a heavy rocket. Both of these are a matter of time, but ‘not essential’. The only thing that truly counts as paradigm-level is reinforcement learning, RL.

points.h: RL is letting AI try random paths by trial and error
points.body: In a 2018 guest lecture at MIT, Ilya summed up reinforcement learning in one sentence: let AI use a random path to try a new task; if the result exceeds expectations, update the neural network's weights so the AI remembers to use this successful practice more, then start the next attempt. Guangmi uses a prospecting metaphor to explain the key to the reward model: one person holds a treasure map, another brings 5,000 special forces soldiers and professional detection equipment — as long as there is treasure, they can almost certainly find it, but if two or three of those special forces are bad at appraising treasure, they will miss the treasure or pick up garbage. That is the reward model making mistakes. Today the industry's reward model is still most core in code and math, because the environment and goals are simple and clear, easy to set up.

points.h: Language is a crutch; reinforcement learning is the main course
points.body: Guangmi offers a vivid metaphor: if language and pretraining are like the human genome, carrying the genes of thousands of years of human evolution, then reinforcement learning is the whole life of human growth, receiving positive and negative signals from the day of birth. Language is the only thing today that has achieved generalization; AlphaGo can only play Go, CV can only do face recognition, neither generalizes. So language and pretraining may just be a crutch, an intermediate dish, an appetizer, and the reinforcement learning that follows is the main course. He judges that today, relying on large language models alone may not reach AGI; AI may be a college student who is lopsided in Chinese, and to get a job a new paradigm needs to be introduced.

points.h: RL trades inference compute for training compute
points.body: Guangmi points out that RL is not a model but a whole system, including agent, environment, action and reward model, and the two most important are the environment and the agent. Its approach in language models is essentially to trade inference time for training time, to solve the current situation where the model's marginal returns are temporarily diminishing as it scales up. He has done the math: for models at the level of GPT-4 and Claude 3.5, synthesizing 1T of high-quality reasoning data costs about $600 million, and synthesizing 10T might cost $6 billion. But inference has relatively lower requirements for single-card performance and cluster scale; you don't necessarily have to use the top cards or 30,000-card or 100,000-card clusters — distributed clusters can also run RL inference.

points.h: Consensus exists only among a few hundred core researchers
points.body: The fact that an AI paradigm shift is happening has, in Silicon Valley, only some consensus among the most core researchers — possibly just a few hundred people — and hasn't fully spread. Many people know RL is important but don't know how to do it, and talent in this area is very scarce; it's not the same batch of people as traditional RL. Guangmi thinks many AI executives may not have realized it yet, because only a small number of papers have recently started coming out. Yann LeCun recently criticized reinforcement learning, saying it wastes resources. Guangmi's response: Edison also wasted a lot of experimental resources inventing the light bulb, but you only need to succeed once and you can replicate it en masse.

points.h: Silicon Valley invests in robot brains, China invests in whole machines
points.body: Guangmi observes that in Silicon Valley everyone now wants to invest in a technical person's brain, wanting to do ROS or Android; in China you invest in the whole machine — OV, Xiaomi. But he raises a paradox: is it possible that there is no such thing as a robot brain, that the brain is just GPT or a general large model, and that building a robot brain may not fit all hardware — data from machine A can't be used on machine B, and it still has to be adapted end-to-end. He believes the most core thing for general robots is still the timing of the technology; a general humanoid explosion may still be five to ten years away, and it's very likely this batch of companies won't truly make it — everyone is still at the research lab stage.

points.h: The hidden line of mobile internet is recommendation; the hidden line of AI is RL
points.body: Guangmi compares mobile internet with today's AI: the visible line of mobile internet was that the world gained four or five billion mobile users; the hidden line was having user behavior data for recommendation — over the past decade, companies that didn't do recommendation didn't grow big. The key feature capabilities were large screens, cameras and GPS, each of which gave birth to very large companies. Today AI's visible line is still the Scaling Law, with Compute at its core; the hidden line may be Self-Play reinforcement learning. He raises a possibility: companies that don't do reinforcement learning today may not make it through the next wave, just like recommendation. The ranking of AI's key capabilities is Coding, multimodality, math, Agent.

quotes.text: Right now we can only say there's a 50% chance that the traditional Scaling Law has already failed. Of course, the other 50% chance is that following the old path can still lead to AGI, right? Keep throwing a hundred thousand cards at it. These two probabilities feel Harvard Harvard.

That is, let AI use a random path to try a new task. If the result exceeds expectations, then update the neural network's weights, let the AI remember to use this successful practice more, and then start the next attempt.
You can compare language and pretraining to the human genome, carrying the genes of thousands of years of human evolution, so reinforcement learning is the whole life of human growth.
Because the idea of RL is essentially to trade inference time for training time, to solve this problem of diminishing marginal returns.
Also wasted a lot of experimental resources, right? But you only need to succeed once, and then you can replicate it en masse.
